title: Operational Compliance and Digital Integration
summary: The concept of licensee obligations has evolved from basic administrative record-keeping and physical warehouse management to a sophisticated digital-first framework. Requirements have shifted from manual audits and physical document production to mandatory integration with Customs Computer Systems, including the use of ESPINs and digital user credentials.

evolution.compliance_mode: From manual/physical record-keeping to digital system integration.
evolution.financial_oversight: From general audit requirements to specific lien bank transaction mandates.

timeline.change: Introduced mandatory annual audits for licensees.
Mandated digital integration (User ID, Password, ESPIN) and formalization of financial transactions through lien banks.
Refined digital access requirements for licensees to include specific Customs Authorities interaction protocols.

member_objects.resolved_text:
১। বিধি ৭ এর পরিবর্তে নিম্নরূপ বিধি ৭ প্রতিস্থাপিত হইবে, যথা :—

“৭। লাইসেন্সের মেয়াদ।—
(ক) লাইসেন্সের মেয়াদ হইবে লাইসেন্স প্রদানের তারিখ হইতে ২(দুই) বৎসর; এবং
(খ) লাইসেন্সীকে প্রতি বৎসর তদসংশ্লিষ্ট প্রতিষ্ঠানের অডিট সম্পন্ন করিতে হইবে।”

Customs License: The license validity period is set at two years from the date of its issuance.
Licensees are required to undergo an annual audit of their relevant institution.

member_objects.clause_title: কাস্টমস কম্পিউটার সিস্টেমের মাধ্যমে কার্য পরিচালনার জন্য ইউজার আইডি, পাসওয়ার্ড ও এজেন্ট নম্বর প্রদান

Customs Computerised System: Licensees are required to obtain a user ID, password, and identification number from the Customs Authority to perform operations such as cargo declaration, clearance, and payment of duties and taxes through this system.
The Customs Authority will grant access to the system only after conducting an inquiry to ensure the licensee possesses the necessary personnel, office equipment, and IT-based infrastructure.

Access to the system may be temporarily deactivated by the Customs Authority without prior notice for reasons such as failure to maintain infrastructure requirements, professional misconduct, inactivity, or involvement in smuggling or tax evasion.
Express Service Providers Identification: Licensees must obtain this unique identification number from the Customs Authority to enable cargo processing and digital interaction with the customs environment.

The identification number is subject to suspension or deactivation by the Customs Authority if the licensee fails to fulfill their responsibilities, neglects license renewal, or engages in illegal activities like duty evasion.
Automated System: Licensees must maintain an automated system capable of connecting with the customs gateway, featuring capabilities for electronic declaration, cargo tracking, data synchronization, and automated issuance of release documents.

The system must support integrated electronic payments for duties and taxes, non-intrusive inspection infrastructure, and provide online portals for customers to track shipments and view transaction histories.
Customs Authority: The Customs Authority is empowered to issue user IDs, passwords, and identification numbers to licensees after verifying their technical and operational compliance.
It holds the authority to investigate licensee facilities and deactivate system access for non-compliance, misconduct, or failure to perform duties.

member_objects.resolved_text: ৪। লিয়েন ব্যাংক।– লাইসেন্সি তাঁহার সকল লেনদেন অনুমোদিত লিয়েন ব্যাংকের মাধ্যমে সম্পাদন করিবেন এবং লিয়েন ব্যাংক অনুমোদন, সংযোজন, বিয়োজন, পরিবর্তন, শাখা পরিবর্তনসহ সংশ্লিষ্ট বিষয়াদি ওয়্যারহাউস লাইসেন্সিং বিধিমালা, ২০২৪ এর বিধান এবং এতদ্বিষয়ে বোর্ড ও লাইসেন্সিং কর্তৃপক্ষ কর্তৃক, সময় সময়, জারীকৃত আদেশ অনুযায়ী ব্যবস্থিত হইবে।

Lien Bank: A licensee is mandated to conduct all their transactions exclusively through an authorized lien bank.
The approval, addition, removal, modification, or change of branches for a lien bank must strictly adhere to the Warehouse Licensing Rules 2024.
The administration and regulation of lien banks are subject to further orders and directives issued by the National Board of Revenue and the licensing authority.
Warehouse Licensing Rules 2024: These rules establish the regulatory framework governing the selection and management of lien banks for licensees.
National Board of Revenue: The National Board of Revenue holds the authority to issue periodic orders and directives that govern the operation and oversight of lien banks used by licensees.
Licensing Authority: The licensing authority is empowered to issue ongoing directives and orders regarding the management and regulatory compliance of lien banks.

member_objects.clause_title: কাস্টমস কম্পিউটার সিস্টেমের মাধ্যমে কার্য পরিচালনার জন্য ইউজার আইডি, পাসওয়ার্ড ও এজেন্ট নম্বর প্রদান

Customs Authority: The Customs Authority is responsible for issuing user IDs, passwords, and the Express Service Providers Identification Number (ESPIN) to licensees for performing customs procedures electronically.
The authority must verify that licensees meet the required infrastructure, equipment, and staffing standards before issuing access credentials to the customs computer system.

The authority has the power to suspend or deactivate a licensee's system access credentials and ESPIN without prior notice if the licensee fails to meet operational requirements, commits misconduct, or engages in smuggling and tax evasion.
Express Service Providers Identification: Licensees must obtain an ESPIN from the Customs Authority to process cargo declarations, customs clearance, duty payments, and delivery tracking within the customs computer system.
Automated System: Licensees are required to maintain an automated system capable of connecting to the customs gateway, which must include features for electronic cargo declaration, non-intrusive scanning, real-time tracking, data synchronization, and automated issuance of release notices.

The automated system must support electronic duty payments, automated invoice generation, maintenance of sender and recipient data, and customer-facing portals for shipment tracking and electronic notification of cargo arrival.
Customs Computerised Entry Processing Sy: This system serves as the central platform for managing the lifecycle of imported consignments, including declaration, valuation, payment of duties and taxes, and delivery to the customer.
